message.content:
Below are two ways you can provision a **Google Cloud Compute Engine** instance that has an NVIDIA RTX A6000 GPU and runs **Ubuntu 20.04 LTS**.

---

## 1️⃣  `gcloud` CLI (recommended)

```bash
# 1. Create a project‑specific zone (replace <PROJECT_ID> & <ZONE>)
gcloud config set project <PROJECT_ID>
gcloud config set compute/zone us-central1-a   # or your preferred zone

# 2. Enable the required APIs (if not already enabled)
gcloud services enable compute.googleapis.com \
                      cloudbilling.googleapis.com \
                      iam.googleapis.com

# 3. Create a service account key (optional but handy for automation)
gcloud iam service-accounts keys create ~/sa-key.json \
    --iam-account=compute-admin@<PROJECT_ID>.iam.gserviceaccount.com

# 4. Create the VM
gcloud compute instances create rtx-a6000-instance \
    --machine-type n1-standard-8 \          # 8 vCPU, 30 GB RAM – adjust as needed
    --image-family ubuntu-2004-lts \        # Ubuntu 20.04 LTS
    --image-project ubuntu-os-cloud \
    --boot-disk-size 100GB \                # size of boot disk
    --boot-disk-type pd-ssd \               # SSD boot disk
    --maintenance-policy TERMINATE \       # terminate on host maintenance
    --restart-on-failure \                 # auto‑restart if it crashes
    --scopes https://www.googleapis.com/auth/cloud-platform \  # full access
    --metadata startup-script='#!/bin/bash
      apt-get update && apt-get install -y cuda-drivers
      echo "Instance ready!"' \            # optional startup script
    --accelerator type=nvidia-tesla-a6000,count=1 \  # add one RTX A6000
    --reservation-affinity=any
```

### What each flag does

| Flag | Purpose |
|------|---------|
| `--machine-type` | CPU/RAM configuration (`n1-standard-8` gives 8 vCPUs + 30 GiB RAM). |
| `--image-family` / `--image-project` | Selects the Ubuntu 20.04 LTS image. |
| `--boot-disk-size/type` | Size & performance of the boot disk. |
| `--maintenance-policy` | How the VM behaves during host maintenance. |
| `--restart-on-failure` | Auto‑restarts the VM if it crashes. |
| `--scopes` | Permissions granted to the VM. |
| `--metadata startup-script` | Bash script that runs at first boot (here we install CUDA drivers). |
| `--accelerator` | Adds GPUs – here one RTX A6000. |
| `--reservation-affinity` | Allows the VM to use preemptible resources if available. |

> **Tip:** If you plan to run GPU workloads, consider installing the NVIDIA driver and CUDA toolkit inside the startup script or via a custom image.

---

## 2️⃣  REST API (JSON payload)

If you prefer to use the raw REST API (e.g., from a CI/CD pipeline), here's a minimal JSON body you can POST to:

```
POST https://compute.googleapis.com/compute/v1/projects/<PROJECT_ID>/zones/us-central1-a/instances
Authorization: Bearer <ACCESS_TOKEN>
Content-Type: application/json
```

### Request Body

```json
{
  "name": "rtx-a6000-instance",
  "machineType": "projects/<PROJECT_ID>/zones/us-central1-a/machineTypes/n1-standard-8",
  "disks": [
    {
      "boot": true,
      "autoDelete": true,
      "initializeParams": {
        "sourceImage": "projects/ubuntu-os-cloud/global/images/family/ubuntu-2004-lts",
        "diskSizeGb": 100,
        "diskType": "projects/<PROJECT_ID>/zones/us-central1-a/diskTypes/pd-ssd"
      }
    }
  ],
  "networkInterfaces": [
    {
      "network": "global/networks/default",
      "accessConfigs": [
        { "type": "ONE_TO_ONE_NAT", "name": "External NAT" }
      ]
    }
  ],
  "metadata": {
    "items": [
      {
        "key": "startup-script",
        "value": "#!/bin/bash\napt-get update && apt-get install -y cuda-drivers\n"
      }
    ]
  },
  "serviceAccounts": [
    {
      "email": "<SERVICE_ACCOUNT_EMAIL>",
      "scopes": ["https://www.googleapis.com/auth/cloud-platform"]
    }
  ],
  "guestAccelerators": [
    {
      "acceleratorCount": 1,
      "acceleratorType": "projects/<PROJECT_ID>/zones/us-central1-a/acceleratorTypes/nvidia-tesla-a6000"
    }
  ],
  "scheduling": {
    "preemptible": false,
    "onHostMaintenance": "TERMINATE",
    "automaticRestart": true
  }
}
```

#### Notes

- Replace `<PROJECT_ID>` with your actual GCP project ID.
- Replace `<SERVICE_ACCOUNT_EMAIL>` with a service account that has the necessary IAM roles (e.g., `roles/compute.admin`, `roles/iam.serviceAccountUser`).
- The `accessToken` can be obtained via OAuth 2.0 or a service account JWT.
- The `guestAccelerators` field attaches the GPU.
- The `metadata.startup-script` installs the NVIDIA driver automatically.

---

## Quick Checklist

| ✅ | Item |
|----|------|
| ✅ | Project & billing enabled |
| ✅ | Compute Engine API enabled |
| ✅ | Service account with `Compute Admin` role |
| ✅ | Proper firewall rules (default allows SSH) |
| ✅ | GPU quota for `nvidia-tesla-a6000` in your region |
| ✅ | Optional: Custom image with pre‑installed CUDA for faster boot |

Once the instance is running, you can SSH into it:

```bash
gcloud compute ssh rtx-a6000-instance
```

And verify the GPU:

```bash
lspci | grep -i nvidia
nvidia-smi
```

That’s it! You now have a fully functional GCE instance equipped with an NVIDIA RTX A6000 GPU and Ubuntu 20.04 LTS.
